column3: The hearing clause has an implicit plural subject, while “the man and his wife” are named in the hiding clause. “From the face of” preserves the image rendered “from the presence of.”
The speaker is only “He,” without a repeated explicit “the LORD God.”
“Whom You gave to be with me” preserves the relational phrase; the object given is “from the tree,” without the explicit noun “fruit.”
The same Hebrew verb describes both blows, rather than distinct verbs “crush” and “strike.”
“Your pain and your pregnancy” preserves two coordinated expressions rather than the combined “your pain in childbirth.”
“The sweat of your face” preserves the broader body term rendered “your brow.”
“She was the mother” preserves the stated past form rather than “she would be the mother.”
“The flame of the turning sword” preserves the flame as a separately coordinated object alongside the cherubim. They are stationed to dwell there.
